system: You are the independent Pattern inducer for an evidence-grounded resolution graph. Use only the supplied training Workflows and Actions. A Pattern is a plain-language cross-project decision policy, not a category label, repository recipe, or claim that different Actions are interchangeable. Preserve distinct Action contracts. Express the reusable structure as role-level action_template entries and bind each supporting Workflow to the exact Action ids that realize those roles. State when to use the Pattern, anti-goals, exclusions, decision branches, ordering, and validation. Use candidate_pending_holdout only when at least two repositories support every required role; it still requires a separate untouched holdout repair. Never invent holdout facts, solution refs, tests, evidence ids, Action ids, or Workflow ids. Return JSON only.

instructions: Give the Pattern a short title a software engineer can understand without knowing AREX.
Describe observable applicability signals, not product names or issue numbers.
Do not merge Actions. Use workflow_realizations to map generic roles to existing ids.
A required role must be independently realized in at least two repositories.
Keep repository-specific branches conditional rather than universally mandatory.
The validation ladder must distinguish focused contract checks, integration checks, and regressions.
If the evidence supports only fragments rather than one coherent policy, return defer.

pattern_candidate.intent: Resolve state continuity and resume through a contract-first, evidence-validated change chain.
pattern_candidate.extraction_method: structural-action-fingerprint-v1; semantic judge required before promotion

workflows.name: resume-persisted-conversation-safely
workflows.title: Resume a persisted conversation without displacing live state or overflowing context
workflows.description: A partial-order startup workflow that reconstructs a persisted transcript only when authoritative live state is absent, then conditionally compacts oversized restored state under both session and model context limits.
workflows.goal: Start a session with usable prior conversational context while preserving explicit caller state and keeping restored history within configured and model-imposed token limits.
when_to_use: A stateful interactive application persists a transcript across process lifetimes and a new session should continue the prior conversation.
The persisted representation contains both conversational content and operational metadata that must not be replayed as model dialogue.
Restored state can be large enough to require compaction before continued use.
anti_goals: Do not replace explicitly supplied in-memory conversation state with disk contents.
Do not replay tool output, session metadata, commands, or blank prompts as conversational messages.
Do not summarize history that already fits the configured retained-history budget.
Do not send an unbounded restored transcript to the summarizer model.
not_applicable_when: The application has no persisted conversation artifact to resume.
The persisted artifact cannot be deterministically mapped to ordered conversational roles.
A caller requires explicit supplied state and persisted state to be merged rather than using explicit state as authoritative.
No reliable token counter or summarizer input limit is available for safe compaction.
inputs: history token budget or model default
workflows.entry_state: Session initialization has begun; completed-message state is either explicitly supplied or empty, and a configured transcript may contain earlier conversation plus operational records.
workflows.exit_state: Explicit completed-message state has been preserved, or persisted conversational messages have been restored; any restored state exceeding its budget has entered bounded compaction, and nonempty restored state is visible through the startup announcement.

steps.condition: Run when completed-message state is empty and the configured transcript contains text.
steps.validation: Verify ordered user/assistant reconstruction and exclusion of recognized metadata, tool output, commands, and blank prompts.

steps.condition: Always enforce precedence; file loading and reconstruction are conditional on the absence of explicit completed-message state.
steps.validation: Verify explicit state is unchanged, while empty state with a populated transcript becomes restored state and produces the restoration announcement.

steps.condition: Evaluate every restored state; start compaction only when its token count exceeds the selected history budget.
steps.validation: Verify threshold behavior and confirm that any summarizer request is restricted to content fitting within the summarizer input limit minus its reserve.

validation_ladder: Unit-check transcript reconstruction with representative user, assistant, session-heading, blockquote, command, and blank-prompt records.
Lifecycle-check precedence using both explicit completed messages and an empty state backed by a populated transcript.
Boundary-check compaction immediately below and above the configured history-token threshold.
Capacity-check that a large selected head is trimmed to the summarizer model's input capacity minus the reserved tokens.
Integration-check that a restarted session reports restoration and can continue using the restored completed-message state.
stop_conditions: Stop restoration and retain explicit state when completed messages were supplied by the caller.
Stop file-based restoration when the configured transcript is absent, unreadable through the input adapter, or empty.
Stop promotion as a fully validated resolution until automated parser, precedence, and compaction tests exist.
Stop or repair if transcript reconstruction cannot preserve conversational ordering or if bounded summarization fails.
unresolved_or_deferred: The pinned change includes no automated tests for transcript parsing, state precedence, startup restoration, token override propagation, or bounded compaction.
The parser does not flush a final accumulated assistant segment at end-of-file, so preservation of a transcript ending directly in assistant content is unresolved.
The standalone aider/history.py entry point calls an undefined summarize_chat_history_markdown method at the pinned ref and therefore is not a usable validation path.

The changed compaction calculation reverses and truncates the sized head before later slicing it with split_index; the exact tail-token accounting should be covered by focused boundary tests before treating it as a proven invariant.

workflows.name: preserve-caller-state-during-resume
workflows.title: Resume from history without corrupting caller-owned state
workflows.description: Establish an ownership boundary for a mutable history passed into a continuation routine, extend only a copied working sequence, and validate both preservation of the input and growth of the returned state.
workflows.goal: Continue an operation from existing history while returning the newly extended history and preserving the caller's original history container.
when_to_use: A continuation or resume API accepts a caller-supplied mutable sequence and appends new state during processing.
Inspection or regression behavior shows that the routine aliases and mutates the caller's non-empty sequence.
anti_goals: Do not remove prior history from the working continuation state.
Do not suppress recording of the new user or assistant messages in the returned state.
Do not deep-copy or transform individual history entries unless nested-entry mutation is separately demonstrated and specified.
not_applicable_when: The API explicitly documents in-place mutation as part of its contract.
The supplied history is immutable or the routine never mutates the sequence structure.
The defect concerns mutation of nested message objects rather than append operations on the outer sequence.
inputs: continuation entry point that accepts prior history
deterministic completion or equivalent response fixture
workflows.entry_state: A non-empty caller-owned history can be bound directly to the routine's working sequence, and later append operations can therefore corrupt the caller's preserved state.
workflows.exit_state: The routine operates on a distinct outer sequence, preserves all supplied history entries for continuation, appends the new turn to the working result, and leaves the caller's input sequence structurally unchanged.

steps.condition: Apply when the continuation routine performs structural mutations such as append on a caller-supplied mutable sequence.
steps.validation: Inspect the initialization boundary and confirm that supplied history is copied into a distinct working sequence before any new-turn append occurs.

steps.condition: Run after the ownership boundary is changed and a deterministic completed-turn fixture is available.
steps.validation: Confirm that the caller's sequence length equals its pre-call baseline and that the returned sequence length exceeds that baseline.

validation_ladder: Static boundary check: the working outer sequence is constructed separately from a supplied mutable history.
Behavioral preservation check: after a completed new turn, the caller's history retains its original length.
Behavioral continuity check: the returned history is longer than the original, proving that isolation did not discard the new turn.
Focused automated regression test when the test runner and dependencies are available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the API contract intentionally transfers ownership and permits in-place mutation.
Stop and broaden the investigation if individual pre-existing message objects are mutated, because a shallow sequence copy does not isolate nested objects.
Defer runtime confirmation if the repository's test runner or required dependencies are unavailable.
unresolved_or_deferred: The committed test checks outer-list length, not object identity, exact preserved contents, or mutation of nested message dictionaries.
A fresh test execution is deferred because pytest is not installed in the supplied environment.

workflows.name: crash-safe-derived-session-publication
workflows.title: Create a derived session without exposing partial state
workflows.description: Plan the entire derived state first, stage it outside the visible destination, and publish it with one atomic filesystem operation.
workflows.goal: A derived persistent session is either complete and reopenable or entirely absent after any reported staging or publication failure.
when_to_use: Creating a new persistent state artifact requires copying multiple entries, pointers, or metadata from an existing session.
The destination can be observed by repository listing or opened while multi-step construction failures are possible.
anti_goals: Do not publish the destination header before all derived mutations are staged.
Do not change which entries, lanes, name, or labels the fork operation selects.
Do not treat deletion of a partially published destination as equivalent to never publishing it.
not_applicable_when: The operation is a normal append to an already published log rather than publication of a new complete artifact.
The filesystem cannot provide same-filesystem atomic rename-with-replacement semantics.
The destination is intentionally designed to expose incremental construction.
inputs: fork scope and optional target position
workflows.entry_state: The source session is loadable, the destination is not published, and fork selection has not yet been materialized as one complete persistence plan.
workflows.exit_state: The destination contains a complete validated fork that reopens with the selected state, or failure leaves neither a visible destination nor a staging artifact.

steps.condition: The persistent backend publishes files through an injected filesystem abstraction.
steps.validation: Replacing an existing file is atomic at the abstraction boundary, and failed rename preserves its destination.

steps.condition: The derived artifact is a session fork selected by tree or branch options.
steps.validation: The plan has consecutive sequence numbers and reconstitutes selected entries, lane pointers, name, and labels while rejecting invalid targets.

steps.condition: A validated plan and destination header are available.
steps.validation: Injected staging and rename failures expose no fork and leave no temporary file; successful publication reopens with complete state.

validation_ladder: Verify atomic replacement semantics and path-aware failure reporting at the filesystem boundary.
Verify successful reopened forks preserve message counts, entries, lanes, name, and labels.
Inject failure during staged mutation writing and verify the fork is not listed and no temporary file remains.
Inject failure during final rename and verify the same absence and cleanup invariants.
stop_conditions: Stop if the complete derived state cannot be determined before writing the destination.
Stop if source and destination cannot reside on a filesystem supporting atomic rename.
Stop and report failure if staging or rename fails; do not expose or continue using the destination.
unresolved_or_deferred: Concurrent publications to the same destination require caller serialization because the implementation uses a deterministic sibling .tmp path.

workflows.name: failure-safe-torn-log-recovery
workflows.title: Recover a torn persistent log without overwriting the original in place
workflows.description: Identify a recoverable incomplete final record, stage the accepted prefix separately, and atomically replace the damaged log only after staging succeeds.
workflows.goal: Restore a replayable log prefix while preserving the original bytes whenever repair publication fails.
when_to_use: Sequential replay succeeds through a valid prefix and only the final physical record is syntactically incomplete.
Repair requires replacing persisted content rather than merely appending a missing newline.
anti_goals: Do not truncate the original file before a complete repaired replacement is ready.
Do not silently repair malformed interior records or semantically invalid complete records.
Do not discard the original error when temporary cleanup runs.
not_applicable_when: The malformed record is not the final physical line.
The final record is complete but violates replay invariants.
The only defect is a valid final line missing its terminating newline and append-only repair is sufficient.
inputs: accepted physical lines forming the valid prefix
workflows.entry_state: The original log remains present, replay has accepted its prefix, and the final physical line has a parse failure with an underlying cause.
workflows.exit_state: The destination contains the valid replayable prefix, or a reported failure leaves the original damaged bytes unchanged and removes the staging file.

steps.condition: Recovery can stage a sibling file on the same filesystem as the session.
steps.validation: Atomic replacement succeeds as one rename event and rename failure leaves existing destination content unchanged.

steps.condition: The parse failure is confined to the final physical line and prior mutations have replayed successfully.
steps.validation: A failed staged repair preserves the original byte sequence and removes the .tmp file; successful repair returns storage representing the accepted prefix.

validation_ladder: Classify the corruption and reject malformed interior or complete semantically invalid mutations.
Verify the computed repair content is exactly the accepted prefix plus a terminating newline.
Inject a staging failure after modifying the temporary file and verify the original bytes remain unchanged.
Verify cleanup removes the sibling temporary file on failure.
stop_conditions: Stop without repair if corruption is not confined to the final physical line.
Stop without repair if replay of any complete preceding mutation fails.
Stop and preserve the original if staging or atomic rename fails.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle contains no CI status or reviewer discussion, so validation is grounded in committed tests rather than recorded test-run results.

workflows.name: preserve-selected-runtime-context-across-session-restore
workflows.title: Preserve workspace runtime context throughout session restoration
workflows.description: A partial-order resolution workflow for restore paths that select the correct workspace runtime explicitly but lose that selection through an ambient storage API during asynchronous load or resume work.
workflows.goal: Ensure every supported cold session load/resume entry point restores persisted state and invokes its bridge under the storage root owned by the selected workspace runtime.
when_to_use: A service supports multiple workspace runtimes or runtime replacement, with separate persisted-session roots.
The restore path passes an explicit runtime root to one service but nested asynchronous restore code also consults an ambient or context-local storage root.
Restoration succeeds in the primary/default workspace but fails, misses state, or observes the wrong root for a secondary or replacement runtime.
anti_goals: Do not merge or relocate session stores between workspace runtimes.
Do not change session identifiers, restore metadata, archive-lock semantics, bridge ownership, or load/resume response shapes.
Do not replace workspace selection logic; preserve the already selected runtime and propagate its storage context.
Do not globally mutate a process-wide storage root when a callback-scoped binding is available.
not_applicable_when: All session storage access is explicitly parameterized and no restore dependency consults ambient runtime state.
The requested session is absent from the correctly selected runtime store rather than hidden by a context mismatch.
The operation creates a new session and does not restore persisted state.
Only one immutable runtime root exists and runtime selection or replacement cannot occur.
inputs: Restore entry points and their load/resume branches
Ambient storage-context API with asynchronous callback propagation
Tests capable of creating distinct runtime roots
workflows.entry_state: Workspace selection returns the intended runtime, and direct service construction may use its root, but the enclosing asynchronous restoration chain can still observe a different ambient storage root.
workflows.exit_state: Every affected load/resume entry point scopes its complete restore critical section to the selected runtime root, and regression tests prove the selected or replacement root is visible at the bridge boundary for both actions.

steps.condition: The product exposes an HTTP session load/resume route that selects among workspace runtimes.
steps.validation: A session stored only beneath a secondary runtime root can be loaded and resumed through HTTP, and the selected bridge observes that root.

steps.condition: The product also exposes ACP or another protocol restore entry point with an independent dispatch path.
steps.validation: After activating a runtime replacement with a distinct root, both protocol load and resume complete without error and the replacement bridge observes its own root.

validation_ladder: Inspect each restore entry point to confirm runtime selection and ambient storage binding cover the same complete asynchronous critical section.
For the HTTP path, store sessions only under a non-default secondary root and verify both load and resume return success while the bridge observes that root.
For the protocol path, activate a replacement runtime with a distinct root and verify both load and resume use the replacement bridge under that root.
Retain existing restore locking, session-resolution, metadata, isolation, ownership, and response behavior inside the scoped callback.
stop_conditions: Stop if the selected runtime does not expose a stable session storage root.
Stop and diagnose runtime-selection logic if the wrong runtime or bridge is chosen before storage scoping begins.
Stop if correct behavior requires moving or sharing persisted state across runtime boundaries; that is a different migration or ownership problem.
Stop if scoping only a synchronous prefix does not propagate through awaited restore work; the context mechanism must support the complete asynchronous callback.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle does not include CI status checks or review discussion.
Tests were inspected as committed regression oracles; no clean test execution result is available from the provided checkout.
ACP is a repository-specific transport instance; applicability to another project requires an equivalent independent restore entry point rather than the same protocol.

actions.intent: Recover replayable state from an incomplete final record without destroying the original session if repair is interrupted.
actions.pre_state: Replay has accepted all preceding mutations and identified a parse failure confined to the final physical line with an underlying parse cause.
actions.post_state: On successful publication the session contains the valid prefix; on staging or rename failure the original bytes remain unchanged and the staging file is removed.
actions.validation: Inject a failure after damaging the staged repair file, then assert open reports a storage error, the original session bytes are unchanged, and no .tmp file remains.
actions.description: Stage the valid JSONL prefix separately and replace the damaged session only after the repaired file is complete.

actions.intent: Determine and validate all state required by a session fork before any destination is published.
actions.pre_state: A valid source session state and fork scope, target entry, and position options are available.
actions.post_state: A consecutively sequenced mutation list represents the selected entries, resulting lanes, optional session name, and labels; an invalid fork target fails before destination publication.
actions.validation: Create and reopen branch and tree forks, then compare message counts, entries, lanes, name, labels, and excluded records with the selected source state.
actions.description: Convert fork selection options and current session state into one ordered mutation plan shared by persistent and in-memory backends.

actions.intent: Prevent cold HTTP load and resume operations from reading or continuing session state under a process-default runtime root when a different workspace runtime was selected.
actions.pre_state: A restore request has selected a workspace runtime whose sessionRuntimeBaseDir may differ from the ambient Storage runtime base directory, while the archive-coordinated asynchronous restore operation is still invoked without an ambient runtime binding.
actions.post_state: The archive-coordinated restore, persisted-session resolution, metadata reads, and selected bridge load/resume call execute with the ambient Storage runtime base directory equal to the selected workspace runtime’s sessionRuntimeBaseDir.
actions.validation: For both load and resume, persist the target session under a secondary runtime root, invoke the HTTP restore route for that workspace, assert success, and assert the selected bridge observes that secondary root through Storage.getRuntimeBaseDir().
actions.description: Bind the full asynchronous HTTP load/resume critical section—not only its SessionService instance—to the selected workspace runtime’s storage root so nested restoration code observes the correct persisted state.

actions.intent: Allow a resumed operation to extend prior state and return the extended state without changing the caller-owned input sequence.
actions.pre_state: A caller may supply a non-empty mutable sequence of prior messages, and the continuation routine will append new-turn messages to its working sequence.
actions.post_state: The continuation routine's outer working sequence is distinct from the supplied sequence; new-turn appends appear in the returned sequence but not in the caller's input list.
actions.validation: Provide a non-empty history, execute a completed new turn, then verify that the input sequence retains its original length while the returned sequence contains additional messages.
actions.description: Create a distinct working sequence at the continuation boundary so additions for the new turn do not alter the caller's historical-state container.

actions.intent: Resume a prior conversation automatically without overwriting authoritative in-memory state supplied by the current caller.
actions.pre_state: A new session has either explicit completed-message state, or an empty completed-message state plus an optional configured persisted transcript.
actions.post_state: Explicit state remains authoritative; otherwise a nonempty persisted transcript becomes the session's completed-message state, and restored state is announced when present.
actions.validation: Initialize once with explicit completed messages and once with an empty state plus a populated transcript; verify the first state is unchanged, the second contains reconstructed history, and the restoration announcement appears only for nonempty completed state. These branches are present in the pinned code but lack an automated regression test.
actions.description: At lifecycle initialization, preserve caller-provided completed messages; otherwise load and reconstruct the configured transcript and expose restoration to the user.

actions.intent: Prevent regression to input-list aliasing while confirming that conversation continuation still records the new turn.
actions.pre_state: A continuation API accepts an existing mutable history and returns a message history after processing another turn.
actions.post_state: The regression oracle demonstrates that the supplied history's outer length is unchanged and the returned history is longer than the original.
actions.validation: Use a deterministic mocked completion, suppress persistence and cleanup side effects, call the continuation API, assert input length equality with the saved baseline, and assert returned length exceeds that baseline.
actions.description: Exercise the continuation boundary with controlled side effects and check both halves of the ownership contract: unchanged caller state and an independently extended result.

actions.intent: Make a prepared file become visible as one replacement event without exposing intermediate destination content.
actions.pre_state: A complete source file and a destination path on a filesystem that supports same-filesystem atomic rename are available.
actions.post_state: On success the source no longer exists and the destination contains the source content; on rename failure the existing destination remains unchanged and the error identifies the failing source when available.
actions.validation: Replace an existing destination and assert the source disappears and new content is visible; inject a missing-source failure and assert the prior destination content remains.
actions.description: Expose a filesystem operation that commits a fully prepared sibling file by atomically replacing the destination and returns structured path-aware failures.

actions.intent: Recover reusable conversational state from a human-readable persisted transcript without replaying operational noise as dialogue.
actions.pre_state: A configured transcript contains interleaved session headings, user headings, assistant text, commands, and blockquoted operational output.
actions.post_state: The transcript is represented as an ordered list of user and assistant message objects, with recognized non-conversational records excluded.
actions.validation: Use a transcript containing each supported record type and verify that ordinary user headings and intervening assistant text are emitted in order while session headings, blockquotes, slash commands, and <blank> prompts are absent. The pinned implementation directly establishes these parsing rules, but the change supplies no automated test oracle.
actions.description: Convert the application's append-only Markdown transcript into model-facing user and assistant messages while excluding session metadata, tool output, commands, and empty prompts.

actions.intent: Keep resumed state usable when persisted history is larger than either the desired conversation budget or the summarizer model's request context.
actions.pre_state: Reconstructed completed messages may exceed the configured history budget, and the portion selected for summarization may exceed the summarizer model's maximum input context.
actions.post_state: History within the configured budget is left intact; oversized history starts compaction, and the summarizer receives the newest portion of the selected head that fits its input limit with a reserve.
actions.validation: Exercise histories below and above the configured budget and use a model with a known max_input_tokens value; verify no worker starts below the threshold, a worker starts above it, and the messages passed to summarization do not exceed max_input_tokens minus 512 according to the implementation's token counter. No such automated test was included in the change.
actions.description: Apply a configurable retained-history budget and bound each summarizer request to the summarizer model's input capacity before background compaction.

actions.intent: Prevent ACP load and resume operations from restoring session state under a stale or default storage root after workspace-runtime selection or replacement.
actions.pre_state: An ACP restore request has resolved a sessionRuntime with its own sessionRuntimeBaseDir, but the asynchronous archive-coordinated restore callback is invoked outside that runtime’s ambient Storage context.
actions.post_state: Persisted-session lookup, metadata recovery, and the selected runtime bridge’s load/resume operation execute while Storage resolves paths from sessionRuntime.sessionRuntimeBaseDir.
actions.validation: For both protocol load and resume, activate a replacement runtime with a distinct storage root, store the session there, issue the request, and assert no protocol error, one restore call, and observation of the replacement root inside the bridge callback.
actions.description: Bind the complete asynchronous ACP load/resume critical section to the selected or replacement workspace runtime so bridge restoration and nested storage access remain aligned with runtime selection.

actions.intent: Prevent incomplete derived sessions from becoming discoverable after interrupted or failed fork creation.
actions.pre_state: A destination header, destination path, and complete validated fork mutation plan exist while the final destination is not yet published.
actions.post_state: Either a complete reopenable fork is present at the destination, or no fork and no staging file is visible after a reported failure.
actions.validation: Inject failures during mutation staging and final rename and assert the fork is absent from repository listing with no .tmp residue; on success reopen and verify all selected state.
actions.description: Build the fork header and all planned mutations in a sibling temporary file, then expose the fork through one atomic replacement and clean up failed staging artifacts.

interpretation.action_reuse: An Action is reusable only when its semantic owner, finite operation, state transition, and validation oracle all survive substitution into the other repository.
interpretation.workflow_reuse: A repeated role sequence such as establish-contract -> reconcile -> validate is a reusable Workflow fragment, but it is a template over new Actions rather than evidence that the Actions themselves are interchangeable.
interpretation.granularity: A split is justified only when a candidate contains independently testable finite operations with separate postconditions or validation oracles. Different paths, providers, or filenames alone are not a reason to split.
